items.headline: Nobel Prize in Medicine awarded for optogenetics, the technique that lets scientists control neurons with light
items.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel won the twenty twenty six Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering light-gated proteins and turning them into switches that control nerve cells. The technique, called optogenetics, has become a standard tool for mapping how the brain shapes memory, mood, and behavior.
items.why_it_matters: Optogenetics has already driven major advances in neuroscience and is being explored to restore vision and treat neurological disease, so honoring it recognizes a tool actively reshaping medicine.
